newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HAVEL CALLS ON BELARUS TO STAY AWAY FROM BRINK.
newsitem.headline: HAVEL CALLS ON BELARUS TO STAY AWAY FROM BRINK.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel called on the Belarussian leadership on Thursday to respect human rights and democracy, and to prevent the former Soviet republic from going towards the brink.

In a statement, Havel expressed his disquiet at the situation in Belarus where President Alexander Lukashenko is locked in a conflict with parliament over a referendum which would give him greater powers.
Havel did not name Lukashenko, who refused to attend a Russian-brokered peace initiative on Wednesday, but his message was clear.
"(Havel) calls on all constitutional actors in the Belarussian republic to (seek) mutual discussions and a resolution of the current conflict," his office said in a statement.

The Belarussian leadership "must defend civic freedom, human rights and democratic principles to which it is bound, and which reflect international norms", said the statement from Havel, a former dissident who spent almost five years in jails before the 1989 fall of Czechoslovak communism.
"Only respect for legal order and democratic fundamentals can allow the current conflict to be overcome and to prevent it moving futher towards the brink," it said.
